name: APB
notes: Recovered by the lead layout — this manual prints its designators before the device rather than after it, which extract_ic_locations could not read until 2026-09. The row states its device twice, as a stock number and in the description, and is taken only when the two agree.
Column-first designators, the post-1983 Atari convention, recorded in grid.transposed rather than inferred: 2L and L2 name the same cell and only the silkscreen says which is printed.
No component-location drawing has been read. The grid spacing is nominal — the designators are real but nothing here has measured the board.
conflicts: 3B is not placed. It reads as the span 3B/F, a device across rows B to F — five rows apart on this grid, where every other span on the board (1B/C, 3C/D, 3F/H, 4E/F) covers two adjacent rows. build_board rejected it rather than drawing a part across five rows. It is most likely an OCR of 3B/C, but that is inference and the map does not carry it.
1 designator rejected as off-grid; 2 rows rejected on the device name.

MAME's ROM map for this machine was NOT applied. MAME names each ROM by the board it sits on, and this hardware is more than one board: MAME puts a ROM at 2B where the parts list reads a 74LS153 — the same cell and the same part as 720 Degrees, which is the same System 2 hardware — and 9 positions fall on rows this map does not have (J, N, S, T). The site's MAME ROM-map page for the machine is unaffected — it never claimed a PCB — but nothing from it is placed on this map until someone attributes MAME's positions to a board.
